answer: Weight influence by verified data availability, not account count. Each worker stores a distinct 1 GB incompressible shard—reef, ocean, or canyon sensor records—and commits its Merkle root. A scheduler samples unpredictable blocks and checks proofs before a deadline; only served shards earn allocation. A thousand aliases therefore require 1 TB of storage plus ongoing bandwidth, so account creation alone buys nothing. This prices capacity, not identity: pooled hardware and wealthy attackers remain possible; security depends on random assignments and deadlines that prevent on-demand fetching.
